title: Rubio, Lavrov Meet in Manila to Revive Stalled Ukraine Peace Talks
excerpt: The two top diplomats met on the sidelines of an ASEAN gathering in the Philippines, with Rubio saying the U.S. remains ready to play a 'constructive role' in ending the war while acknowledging that no quick deal is in sight.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Rubio and Lavrov met in Manila to discuss the Ukraine conflict amid global tensions.
  • Rubio emphasized U.S. readiness to help but warned of slow progress in peace talks.
  • Lavrov reiterated Russia's commitment to proposals from the Trump-Putin summit in 2025.
  • The ASEAN summit was overshadowed by the U.S.-Iran conflict and energy market disruptions.
  • India's role in U.S.-Russia diplomacy was highlighted during the meeting.
Diplomatic Engagement Amid Global Tensions
›Rubio and Lavrov met on ASEAN sidelines.
›Rubio described the war as 'senseless' and 'bloody'.
›Lavrov reaffirmed Russia's commitment to Anchorage proposals.
›ASEAN summit focused on multiple geopolitical crises.
Source: Article on Rubio-Lavrov meeting

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov held face-to-face talks in Manila on Thursday, the highest-level U.S.-Russia diplomatic engagement on the Ukraine war in months. The meeting came on the sidelines of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations Regional Forum, where dozens of foreign ministers gathered amid escalating crises in the Middle East and the South China Sea.

Rubio said afterward that President Donald Trump had made clear the United States was prepared to help facilitate an end to what he called a "senseless war," but tempered expectations about the pace of any resolution.

"I think it is a very bloody war. I think both sides should have an incentive to bring it to an end. That's been the challenge, is an end that both sides can accept, and we've tried, and we'll continue to try to see if we can find a middle ground that brings this about."

— Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State

He described the session as "a good conversation, a frank conversation" but declined to reveal specifics of what was discussed, saying only that Washington had conveyed its position to Moscow.

Russia Points to Anchorage Framework

Lavrov, according to a statement from the Russian Foreign Ministry, "reaffirmed Russia's readiness for a political and diplomatic settlement of the conflict" and told Rubio that Moscow remained committed to proposals put forward by Presidents Trump and Vladimir Putin at their August 2025 summit in Anchorage, Alaska.

During the meeting, Lavrov briefed Rubio on the situation along the combat line and stressed the importance of halting arms supplies to Ukraine, according to the Russian state news agency TASS. The two diplomats also discussed normalizing operations at their respective diplomatic missions and addressed regional issues, including the conflict in West Asia, TASS reported.

The framing of the Anchorage summit has been a persistent sticking point. Rubio has previously said no final agreement on Ukraine was reached in Alaska, while Lavrov countered in June that American proposals were "discussed" and "accepted by the Russian side," calling Rubio's characterization less than "elegant."

ASEAN Gathering Under Shadow of Multiple Crises

The Rubio-Lavrov meeting unfolded at a Manila summit already overshadowed by the U.S.-Iran conflict and its disruption to global energy markets. The U.S. military completed a 12th successive night of strikes on Iran earlier this week, while Iranian-aligned Houthis claimed hits on two Saudi oil tankers — a blockade threatening a second chokehold on global oil supplies alongside the Strait of Hormuz, according to Reuters.

ASEAN's combined GDP of roughly $3.8 trillion is heavily reliant on Middle East oil, and Philippine Foreign Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro warned that ministers were convening "against the backdrop of profound geopolitical and geoeconomic uncertainty."

Rubio's schedule in Manila was packed. He held a 90-minute meeting with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi to discuss trade, Taiwan, and potential areas of cooperation ahead of President Xi Jinping's planned visit to Washington. He also joined counterparts from India, Australia, and Japan for a session of the Quad grouping.

India's Role on the Margins

U.S. Ambassador to India Sergio Gor was present at the Rubio-Lavrov meeting, according to IANS, a detail that highlights the intersection of U.S.-Russia diplomacy with Washington's relationship with New Delhi. India has maintained ties with both Moscow and Washington throughout the war and has repeatedly called for a resolution through dialogue. The Quad session at the same gathering further underscored India's role as a key stakeholder in the broader diplomatic equation around the conflict.

What's Next

Both sides agreed to continue contacts between their foreign ministries, including within international organizations. But the gap between Russia's insistence that the Anchorage proposals were accepted and Rubio's position that no final deal was reached suggests that bridging the divide will require more than side-of-summit conversations. For now, Washington appears to be signaling engagement without committing to a specific timeline or framework for negotiations.
